label: PF Backlog 438
title: Bmig: migrate high-value legacy Python -> Go (by value)

analysis.implementation_strategy: Follow the BI-PF-0386 value-assessment ranking: migrate modules ranked HIGH value from Python to Go, one module per PR. Start with core/persona.py (already flagged as candidate) by porting its logic to Go while keeping the existing Python API contracts (/api/v1/portfolio/supervisor/*) unchanged. config/legacy-frozen.json and config/persona.json must remain loadable by both runtimes during transition. Go binaries replace .py files per the BI-PF-0387 baseline (no raw .py at customer). Do NOT migrate low-value modules (those stay Nuitka-compiled).
dependency_findings: REQUIRES: BI-PF-0386 — value-ranking output must exist before migration order is determined.
RELATED: BI-PF-0387 — policy baseline (Go for high-value, Nuitka for rest) governs this item.
RELATED: BI-PF-0406 — Go service binaries may become decomposed service boundaries.
RELATED: BI-PF-0405 — WASM plugins may overlap with Go runtime embedding.
conflict_findings: core/persona.py is touched by any agent-persona work concurrent in the queue — serialize migration against those.
Supervisor APIs (/api/v1/portfolio/supervisor*) must keep identical request/response contracts while backend switches language — any concurrent API change conflicts.
config/persona.json and config/legacy-frozen.json are shared config files — migration must not break Python fallback loader.
duplication_findings: BI-PF-0386 (IP-value assessment) is a hard prerequisite — migration order must come from its ranking, not be invented here.
BI-PF-0387 (platform delivery baseline) already settles the 'compile everything, Go for high-value' policy — do not restate, just follow.
core/persona.py is also a candidate in other AI/agent items — confirm no concurrent rewrite planned.
analysis.rationale: The item is a directive to execute a migration whose target order comes from BI-PF-0386. core/persona.py is the only concrete Python component named in candidate code. Confidence is low because the ranking artifact (BI-PF-0386) has not been delivered and the interop/cutover strategy is unsettled. Rewrite is required (Python→Go) but reuse applies to API contracts and JSON configs.
assumptions: BI-PF-0386 ranking will identify core/persona.py as high-value (it is listed as a candidate here, but confirmation pending).
Go toolchain will be adopted as a first-class build dependency per BI-PF-0387.
API contracts (/api/v1/portfolio/supervisor*) remain stable during migration.
config JSON formats are runtime-agnostic and readable from Go without change.
A parity test harness will be used to validate Go output vs Python output on the same inputs.
risks: Behavioral drift between Python and Go implementations (subtle differences in serialization, error handling).
Python↔Go interop during transition adds complexity (subprocess, FFI, or sidecar).
Dependency on BI-PF-0386 ranking being completed and accurate.
Go runtime adds a second toolchain to maintain.
Regression risk to persona.py behavior used by downstream agents.
evidence: Candidate code: core/persona.py; supervisor APIs; persona.json and legacy-frozen.json configs
BI-PF-0387 policy text explicitly directs new high-value logic to Go.

Who owns Go toolchain setup and CI for the Go build.
Parity-test scope and golden-input corpus definition.
